title: commit-aware-proportional-shedder-and-guaranteed-throughput-allocator
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Customers on Dedicated capacity have surface-level SLAs expressed as committed throughput plus burst headroom. Current eviction/shedder behavior is reactive and can cause unfair burst exhaustion where recently active tenants consume disproportionate soft-burst, leading to prompt tail latencies for long-running tenants. This PR implements two coordinated pieces: a commit-aware proportional shedder (CAPS) and a guaranteed-throughput allocator (GTA).

Motivation: provide stronger probabilistic guarantees for committed throughput, reduce microburst-driven unfairness, and expose telemetry that explains observed latency spikes.

Design summary:
1) CAPS - a tenant-aware shedder that makes admission decisions using a 2-window state: (a) committed-window tracks pledged capacity consumption and leaks credits according to commit rate; (b) smoothing-window observes short-term burst usage. Admission score = alpha * committed_score + (1-alpha) * burst_score, where alpha is configurable per-tenant. When admission fails, the shedder prefers delta-shed (delay) over hard-drop when backlog latency budgets exist.

2) GTA - a background allocator that periodically (tick=250ms) assigns soft headroom across tenants using proportional weighting by (commit_fraction * long_term_weight + recent_utilization_weight). GTA reserves a safety-margin computed from tail-percentile of observed per-tenant hotspots to guarantee a high-probability floor for committed throughput.

3) Telemetry - new metrics: tenant_commit_credit{tenant}, tenant_burst_index{tenant}, tenant_headroom_reserved{tenant}, global_shed_rate, allocator_decision_latency. Also added histograms for per-tenant P50/P95/P99 observed commit consumption.

4) Controls - config knobs exposed via dedicated-config v2 schema: commit_window_secs, smoothing_window_secs, alpha_override, safety_margin_percentile, allocator_tick_ms.

5) Rollout - feature-flagged; default off. Canary step targets 10 dedicated pools across two regions, then staged ramp to 50% of dedicated capacity with a 7-day observation window.

Implementation notes:
- The shedder is implemented in runtime/admission/caps_shedder.go and includes a compact circular buffer for commit-window accounting to minimize GC pressure.
- The allocator lives in controllers/dedicated/guaranteed_allocator.go and interfaces with the existing reservation reconciler.
- Telemetry hooks added in observability/metrics_registry.go and wire-compatible with Console dashboards.

Backwards compatibility: config schema extends dedicated-config; defaults keep current behavior when feature flag disabled.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for admission heuristics and allocator balancing (runtime/admission/caps_shedder_test.go, controllers/dedicated/guaranteed_allocator_test.go).
- Simulation harness changes in benchmark-lab/simulations/commit_burst_sim.go to reproduce unfair-burst scenarios.
- Load tests: canary-run results (summary below) were observed on a 16-node dedicated pool: with CAPS+GTA enabled, median committed-serving latency improved 12%, P95 improved 7%, burst exhaustion events reduced from 18/hour to 3/hour.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests on staging
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards
- [x] Documentation: /docs/dedicated/commit-aware-shedder.md
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollback path described

Rollout plan: 1) Canary 10 pools (48h) 2) Ramp to 30% (72h) 3) Full rollout with throttled ramp and automated rollback trigger if global_shed_rate > 2x baseline or allocator_decision_latency > 200ms for >5m.

Notes: We intentionally keep the committed credit leak conservative to avoid stealing headroom from low-burst tenants. The allocator also exposes a dry-run mode (metrics-only) to validate decisions without mutating reservations.

Related: builds on ENG-3121 (reservation telemetry) and complements PR ENG-1127 (fairness scheduler refactor).
